title: What every capture must look like — pinned BEFORE the capture was taken
pinned_from: the Week 10 league report structure as published on nfl.com, cross-checked against the two peer captures already in this repository (nfl-availability-desk/data/drift_expectations.json and nfl-book/data/injuries_week10_capture.json) — no number here is invented
why: The brief's alarm: 'Add a drift alarm to every scraper — pin each parser to expected row counts and required fields; fail the build loudly when a field goes missing rather than publishing a blank.' These pins are the collector's tripwires; engine/drift.py enforces them on every capture, session or CI.

league_injury_report.note_on_anchors: the exact row/club/section counts and the practice-status tally are pinned to the Week 10 report as published; a future capture of a DIFFERENT week legitimately differs, so a CI capture of another week validates structure (fields, vocabulary, floor) and records counts without failing on the Week 10 anchors — the anchors are enforced only for captures whose source URL or week control says Week 10

league_transactions.note: the November 2026 trades view printed a blank Position cell on every row; blank is preserved, never filled

league_reserve_list.coverage_note_pinned: the rendered November table begins at 11/07; IR placements dated 11/05-11/06 are not visible in the rendered view and are never filled from another source

club_depth_gb.club_self_label_required: the page's own status line must be captured verbatim (as published it reads 'Unofficial, Nov. 10, 2026'); a capture missing that line fails
club_depth_gb.jersey_strip_rule: leading digits before the first space become jersey_number; the remainder is the name; raw_cell always keeps the printed string
club_depth_gb.no_rank_inference: slot numbers are the printed column positions (1/2/3) of the club's own table; the collector adds no rank the page does not print and no starter/backup label of any kind

peers.read_window_utc: 2026-11-16 (window recorded by that session; per-call clocks not exposed by its fetch path)

cross_capture_reconciliation.rule: every (team, player_slug) key must reconcile field-by-field against each peer capture; any difference is published on the captures page, never silently resolved

club_code_aliases.why: the nfl-book peer capture normalizes the Cardinals code to ARI; the live page and the availability-desk peer print AZ. The alias is applied ONLY inside cross-capture reconciliation so the comparison can proceed; published rows always keep the code exactly as the page printed it
